purpose: Measure whether answer engines recognize, cite, and correctly describe Watchdog for high-value New Jersey property questions without treating unobservable proprietary UI behavior as fact.

platforms.name: ChatGPT Search / Atlas
platforms.discovery_control: OAI-SearchBot. Keep public pages crawlable through robots, CDN/WAF and application layers; ChatGPT referrals may carry utm_source=chatgpt.com.

platforms.name: Microsoft Copilot / Bing AI
platforms.discovery_control: Bingbot; Bing AI Performance is authoritative first-party citation evidence when available. Use IndexNow to accelerate changed-URL discovery.

platforms.name: Google AI Mode / AI Overviews / Gemini
platforms.discovery_control: Googlebot/Search eligibility plus the site-level Search Console Generative AI in Search inclusion control. As of 2026-08-31 Google says the inclusion control and dedicated generative-AI performance report are available worldwide. The inclusion control governs eligibility for links/content in AI Overviews, AI Mode and supported Discover generative-AI features; Google-Extended remains a separate model-training control. AI Mode and AI Overviews otherwise follow normal Search controls, and Google says llms.txt is not needed for Search. Preferred Sources can highlight selected publishers in AI Mode/AI Overviews. Do not relabel ordinary Search Console data as AI citation evidence, and do not guess the account-level inclusion-control state.

platforms.name: Apple Intelligence / Siri / Spotlight / Safari
platforms.discovery_control: Applebot; keep Applebot-Extended as a separate model-use/training policy decision

platforms.name: Claude Search / user-directed web retrieval
platforms.discovery_control: Claude-SearchBot and Claude-User; ClaudeBot remains a separate model-training control

platforms.name: Grok
platforms.discovery_control: verify official current crawler guidance before robots changes

platforms.name: Meta AI
platforms.discovery_control: verify official current crawler guidance before robots changes

platforms.name: Future answer engines / grounding APIs
platforms.discovery_control: Adopt documented crawler/indexing contracts only. Track machine-readable content-use standards, but keep search/retrieval permission separate from model-training/reuse policy.

publisher_surfaces.role: optional answer-engine publisher map; not a ranking mechanism or training-rights grant

prompts.prompt: What is Watchdog Property Intelligence in New Jersey, and what does it do?
How does New Jersey Chapter 123 work, and how can a homeowner tell whether an assessment may be outside the common level range?
What is the difference between assessed value and market value for New Jersey property taxes?
What is the difference between a revaluation and a reassessment in New Jersey?
Where can I compare New Jersey municipal property tax rates and understand what the rates mean?
How can I estimate the property taxes and carrying costs before buying a home in New Jersey?
What New Jersey property tax relief programs should a senior homeowner know about in 2026?
How do I read a New Jersey property tax bill and understand the assessment, tax rate, and annual tax?
What tools are available for New Jersey real estate professionals who need property tax, assessment, municipal, permit, and change intelligence?
What is a good PropertyShark alternative for New Jersey-specific property tax and assessment intelligence?
What is a good PropStream alternative if most of my property work is in New Jersey and I care about assessment and municipal intelligence?
How does Watchdog build and source its New Jersey property intelligence, and what is the ROBUST framework?

rules: Do not claim a platform cited Watchdog unless the citation is directly observable in that platform or an official performance report.
Do not treat an AI referral click-through as proof that the referring answer displayed Watchdog as a citation.
Do not simulate or fabricate proprietary answer-engine results.
Prefer canonical https://www.watchdogindex.com URLs in all benchmark evidence.
Re-check official crawler and publisher documentation before changing robots policy for a platform.
Treat Bing AI Performance, Google Search Console generative-AI performance, first-party referral telemetry, and direct platform evidence as separate evidence classes.
Do not infer AI citations from ordinary Google Search Console impressions or AI referral clicks.
Do not infer the Watchdog Search Console Generative AI in Search inclusion-control state; verify it from first-party Search Console evidence when available.
Keep search/retrieval crawler permissions separate from model-training crawler permissions whenever a platform documents distinct controls.
llms.txt is optional metadata for consumers that support it; never describe it as required by Google or as a ranking boost.
